goal: Substantively rewrite the existing v3.2 X Article as v3.3 to remove formulaic AI cadence, strengthen authorial judgment and preserve the approved thesis, seven-section structure and single Bigfoot metaphor.
audience: Crypto-native X readers and Solana/memecoin market participants who value a sharp, nuanced argument about cultural contribution, token ownership and cash-flow rights.

content_contract.title_en: When Everyone Has a Bag, Who Do You Believe?
content_contract.title_zh: 当所有人都有仓位，你还能相信谁？
content_contract.subtitle_en: Everyone can make a meme famous. Not everyone gets paid when its token runs.
content_contract.approved_thesis: Financial incentives make public conviction an ambiguous signal.
content_contract.keyword_rule: Use Bigfoot exactly once in Section 01 of each language as a metaphor. Do not explain Bigfoot or create a new topic, event, token or case study.
content_contract.revision_rule: A structural and voice rewrite is authorized. Preserve title, subtitle, approved thesis, seven-section structure, five article source URLs and the single Bigfoot metaphor per language. Refresh dependent distribution and visual/layout assets where the revised manuscript requires it.

hard_constraints: Continue the existing article; do not create a new article.
Do not turn Bigfoot into a topic, factual case, event or token discussion.
Do not change the English/Chinese titles, English subtitle, approved thesis, seven-section structure or five article source URLs.
Do not add unsupported claims, imply wallet classifications are verified identities, or treat first sale as proof of a complete exit.
Do not represent the Dogesled fundraiser as proof of fair token pricing.
Do not claim that sincere holders are necessarily neutral or that financial incentives prove dishonesty.
Do not modify the CAOS parent system or IPOS.
Do not modify main, merge a branch or publish to X.
Do not claim independent review, target-reader validation, rights approval or X-native preview unless evidenced.
Do not claim image generation; this delivery contains prompts and placements only.
success_criteria: Bigfoot appears exactly once in each language.
Both manuscripts retain seven sections and the same five article source URLs.
English word count is reduced by approximately 20–30% versus v3.2 without deleting necessary evidence.
Each section advances a distinct part of the argument; repeated mini-conclusions and stock transitions are materially reduced.
The author expresses a concrete position through reader tests and judgments rather than self-announcing phrases.
English reads as natural crypto-native X Article prose; Chinese is a faithful, idiomatic adaptation rather than a sentence-by-sentence calque.
Distribution copy is refreshed and each standalone post/thread item is under 280 characters.
Visual prompt pack specifies one 5:2 cover and three 16:9 inline visuals, placements, captions, alt text and manual data-card caveats.
DOCX/PDF copies are generated, hyperlinks are preserved and rendered pages are visually checked.
The complete ZIP passes integrity checks and the asset manifest contains SHA-256 hashes.
The Video Studio runtime accepts the brief and dynamic task graph.

governance_boundary.decision_method: CAOS session-level decision governance: competing hypotheses, root-cause diagnosis, alternative comparison, falsifier, execution checks and evidence-bound acceptance.
governance_boundary.child_runtime: Video Studio remains standalone as declared by its own runtime contract; CAOS runtime dependency remains false.
